extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency NEPA program staff, agency legal and policy officials, and public stakeholders (including commenters and project sponsors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for Federal agencies to develop, update, and implement NEPA procedures, including public engagement roles, categorical exclusions, document integrity, review timelines, and use of agency websites. Targets agency NEPA program design and implementation to conform with CEQ's final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Chief Public Engagement Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify a Chief Public Engagement Officer (CPEO) as required in §1507.2(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies the CPEO is responsible for facilitating community engagement in environmental reviews and the regulation does not make the officer responsible for all engagement across the agency; agencies have discretion to define the role more broadly. When an agency is a department, major subunits may designate senior officials or CPEOs, with department-level official having oversight. A senior agency official must be an official of assistant secretary rank or higher (or equivalent) or have equivalent authority in a subunit. Agencies may designate current employees to serve and need not hire new staff. CEQ may provide non-regulatory guidance on duties but declined to specify detailed responsibilities in the regulation; removed duplicative phrasing (“Agencies shall”). Comments about potential overlap with other positions (e.g., CERPO) and resource burdens were considered in finalizing the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare environmental documents with professional and scientific integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to prepare environmental documents with professional integrity consistent with section 102(2)(D) of NEPA (codified as a new paragraph (e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized this provision as proposed; no substantive comments were received on this change. The requirement emphasizes professional and scientific integrity in preparation of EAs and EISs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reliable data and resources in environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must make use of reliable data and resources, consistent with section 102(2)(E) of NEPA (codified as a new paragraph (f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized as proposed; intended to ensure analyses rely on reliable information sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must study, develop, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives consistent with section 102(2)(F) of NEPA (codified as a new paragraph (g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized as proposed; intended to ensure that alternatives analysis addresses technically and economically feasible options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to submit proposed agency procedures to CEQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have 12 months after the final rule effective date to develop proposed NEPA procedures and initiate consultation with CEQ (§1507.3(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to change the 12-month period despite comments that it may be insufficient; agencies need only provide CEQ with proposed revisions within 12 months (not finalized procedures). CEQ will work with agencies to update procedures as quickly as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance or update of agency NEPA procedures not subject to NEPA review
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuance of new agency procedures or updates to existing agency procedures is not itself subject to NEPA review (new paragraph (b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as consistent with longstanding practice; CEQ added this clarification without receiving comments on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should designate major decision points and start NEPA early
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures should designate the major decision points for programs and actions subject to NEPA and ensure the NEPA process begins at the earliest reasonable time (modification to paragraph (c)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ made a clarifying edit to emphasize early integration of NEPA into decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include environmental documents, comments, and responses in administrative records for rulemakings and adjudications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures should make relevant environmental documents, comments, and responses part of the record in both rulemakings and adjudicatory proceedings (modification to paragraph (c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ removed the word “formal” and clarified agencies should include these materials in the record for both rulemakings and adjudicatory proceedings to ensure decisionmakers have access to NEPA information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate environmental review into agency decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures should integrate environmental review so decisionmakers use the information when making decisions (modification to paragraph (c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change was made for clarity and conciseness; agencies should ensure environmental analyses are usable by decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine environmental documents to facilitate efficient decisionmaking and avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining environmental documents should be done to facilitate sound and efficient decision making and avoid duplication (modification to paragraph (c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ struck language that allowed agencies to substitute other reviews as functionally equivalent to NEPA. The intent is to combine documents where consistent with applicable statutory requirements and to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous review and revision of agency NEPA policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must continue to review their policies and procedures and revise them as necessary to be in full compliance with NEPA (restoration of 1978 regulation language in paragraph (b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ restored this longstanding requirement despite comments that it would cause instability; CEQ considers periodic review important to ensure procedures meet NEPA intent and reflect changes in authority or programs. This requirement is distinct from the initial 12-month update requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and substantiate categorical exclusions (CEs) and identify extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish CEs and identify extraordinary circumstances, and provide a process for establishing new or revising existing CEs, including when documentation is required (moved to paragraph (c)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed (and finalized with clarifying edits) that agencies identify when documentation is required for a CE determination, substantiate new or revised CEs with sufficient information to conclude the category does not have a significant effect individually or in the aggregate, and describe how they will consider extraordinary circumstances when applying CEs. Agencies are not required to document and publish all CE determinations (CEQ declined to impose that burden) but must identify which CEs require documentation and whether to make that documentation public. CEQ cross-references §1501.4(b) for the process regarding extraordinary circumstances and documents when a CE applies despite extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate that CEs do not have significant effects individually or in the aggregate
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing or revising a CE, agencies must substantiate with sufficient information that the category of actions does not have a significant effect, individually or in the aggregate (paragraph (c)(8)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined suggestions to add categorical exclusions for historically controversial or environmentally justice–sensitive categories into the regulation itself, instead requiring substantiation on a case-by-case basis and public availability of supporting information for new/revised CEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use phrasing “individually or in the aggregate” for CE significance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text uses the term “individually or in the aggregate” rather than “cumulative” to describe CE significance determinations, consistent with §1501.4 and to avoid confusion with the definition of “effects.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to replace the phrase with “cumulative,” noting that “in the aggregate” has the same meaning as the 1978 regulation’s “individually or cumulatively.” The choice avoids overlap with the definition of effects that includes cumulative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of CEs at least every 10 years
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must include in their NEPA procedures a process for reviewing their CEs at least every 10 years (new paragraph (c)(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed a 10-year minimum (guidance previously recommended 7 years) because reviews can take about a year to complete; agencies may review CEs on a rolling basis and should prioritize oldest CEs first. CEQ declined to require notice-and-comment for reviews themselves but noted that revisions to CEs would require notice-and-comment under §1507.3(b) or §1501.4(c). CEQ clarified that periodic review has no implications for prior CE determinations (does not reopen approvals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include processes for reevaluation and supplementation of EAs and EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures must include processes for reevaluating and supplementing EAs and EISs, as appropriate (moved to §1507.3(c)(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised wording to refer to “processes for” reevaluation and supplementation to provide agencies flexibility to develop procedures consistent with longstanding practice and §1502.9(e). This provision addresses the ability to introduce supplemental analyses into administrative records as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information on where to obtain EIS/EA and NEPA process information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency NEPA procedures must explain where interested persons can get information on EISs, EAs, and the NEPA process (moved to §1507.3(c)(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added reference to EAs as well as EISs; no comments were received on this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for applicant- or project sponsor‑prepared EAs and EISs (minimum requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, agencies must include procedures to allow applicants or project sponsors to prepare EAs and EISs consistent with §1506.5, and set minimum requirements for such procedures (added as §1507.3(c)(12) with subparagraphs (i)–(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised language to apply where an agency has applicants seeking its action. Minimum requirements added: (i) agency procedures must provide for agency review and approval of the purpose and need and alternatives; (ii) agency must independently evaluate applicant-prepared documents, take responsibility for accuracy, scope, and contents, and document that evaluation consistent with §1506.5(a); (iii) applicants cannot prepare Findings of No Significant Impact (FONSIs) or Records of Decision (RODs). CEQ declined to add additional public-engagement requirements specific to applicant-prepared documents because existing regulations already require public engagement in EA and EIS preparation. CEQ also clarified that these procedures do not apply when an applicant serves as a joint lead agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures should include assistance to applicants (per §1501.2(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency NEPA procedures should address assistance to applicants consistent with §1501.2(b)(4) (moved into consolidated paragraph (c)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed paragraph (c)(6) addressed procedures required by §1501.2(b)(4) regarding assistance to applicants; CEQ moved and revised such content for readability and consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must identify typical classes of actions that normally require EISs or EAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures should identify typical classes of actions or common activities that normally require an EIS or EA (paragraphs (c)(7) and (c)(7)(i)/(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions date back to 1978 and are intended to put the public on notice of the decisions agencies regularly make that require these levels of NEPA review; lists are not determinative for any particular action and CEQ did not intend the edits to change thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional items agencies may include in procedures (including emergency and classified actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ provides a list of items agencies may include in their procedures, as appropriate, including identifying activities or decisions not subject to NEPA, processes for emergency actions that would not result in significant environmental effects, and handling of classified proposals (paragraph (d) and subparagraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized this as an optional list because items will not always be applicable to every agency. For emergency actions, agencies may consider special arrangements for EAs (format, distribution, public involvement, timing). For classified proposals, CEQ expects agencies to withhold only what is necessary and structure documents so unclassified portions can be made available for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should use websites and information technology tools to promote NEPA transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to provide on their websites or through other information technology tools their agency NEPA procedures and a list of EAs and EISs that are in development and complete; CEQ encourages agencies to post environmental documents (§1507.4(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised wording to say “other information technology tools” and removed the adjective “environmental” before “documents” when referring to NEPA-related information broadly. Posting of documents is encouraged rather than required; agencies should use IT to promote transparency and efficiency in the NEPA process.
